questions.text: An architect is designing a 15-story mixed-use building with both office and storage spaces on multiple floors. For a floor plan that places a Group D storage room directly below a Group B office suite, the fire-rated floor assembly between them must provide a minimum fire rating of:

rationale.a: 1-hour is insufficient for storage occupancy separation.
rationale.c: 3-hour is not required for this occupancy mix.
rationale.correct: Vertical occupancy separation follows the same requirements as horizontal separation. Group D storage requires a 2-hour separation from Group B per PD 1096.
rationale.takeaway: Separation ratings apply to both walls and floor/ceiling assemblies. Group D vs Group B = 2-hours.

questions.text: An architect is revising a mixed-use building design to correct fire-safety deficiencies. The current plan shows: (1) Group D storage separated from Group B office by a 1.5-hour wall, (2) a central exit stairwell with 1.5-hour wall rating, and (3) a Group G chemical storage room separated from adjacent Group B space by a 2-hour wall. How many of these three separations are non-compliant with Philippine codes?

options.text: Zero—all three are compliant, meeting the minimum fire-resistance requirements
One separation is non-compliant, requiring additional fireproofing measures
Two separations are non-compliant, necessitating a redesign of the fire safety plan

rationale.a: All fail to meet the minimum standards of PD 1096 and RA 9514.
rationale.d: Correct. 1.5-hour is too low for Storage and Stairs (2hr), and 2-hour is too low for Group G (4hr).
rationale.correct: All three fail minimum requirements: (1) Group D requires 2-hours; (2) Multi-story exit stairs require 2-hours; (3) Group G requires 4-hours.
rationale.takeaway: ALE Essentials: Corridor=1hr; Storage/Stairs=2hr; Hazardous=4hr. Anything less is a violation.

questions.code_citation: PD 1096 Rule VII Table VII.4, RA 9514 IRR Rule 10

questions.text: An interior finish schedule for a 2-hour fire-rated wall shows gypsum wallboard without joint taping or finish. Is this assembly compliant with fire-rating requirements?

options.text: Yes, gypsum board alone provides fire rating, which is a common misconception in fire safety design.
No, joint taping and finish coating must be applied to achieve the rated assembly.
No, fire-rated walls must be solid concrete or masonry, which are inherently more fire-resistant.
Yes, but only if the wall is sprinklered, which can compensate for the lack of joint treatment.

rationale.a: The gypsum core provides the rating, but the seams are the point of failure if not taped.
rationale.c: Drywall assemblies are permitted fire-rated systems if constructed per tested specifications.
rationale.d: Sprinklers do not waive the requirement for proper assembly construction.
rationale.correct: Fire-rated gypsum assemblies are tested as a complete system per ASTM E119. Joint treatment (tape and compound) is required to prevent fire from bypassing the gypsum layers at the seams.
rationale.takeaway: Fire rating refers to an 'assembly', not just a material. All components including fasteners and tape must be present.

questions.text: A corridor in an office building serves multiple tenant spaces. According to RA 9514, what is the minimum fire rating for the corridor walls separating it from the occupied spaces?

options.text: No rating required; corridors are common areas.

rationale.a: Common area corridors must be rated to protect the path of travel for occupants of multiple suites.
rationale.c: 1.5-hour is for specific door openings, not standard corridor walls.
rationale.d: 2-hour is for vertical exits (stairs) or storage separation.
rationale.correct: Corridors used as an exit access shall be separated from other parts of the building by walls having a fire resistance rating of at least 1 hour.
rationale.takeaway: The baseline fire rating for an exit access corridor is 1-hour.

questions.text: An exit door opening into a 2-hour rated exit stairwell enclosure must have a minimum fire rating of:

rationale.a: 20-minute doors are for smoke partitions, not exit enclosures.
rationale.c: 1.5-hour is an international standard but 1-hour is the recognized minimum in the local context for these openings.
rationale.d: The door rating is usually less than the wall rating due to the limited area of the opening.
rationale.correct: According to the Fire Code and PD 1096, doors in a 2-hour fire-rated enclosure typically require a 1-hour or 1-1/3 hour (80 min) fire protection rating.
rationale.takeaway: Exit doors in 2-hour stairwells require a 1-hour fire rating.

questions.code_citation: RA 9514 IRR Rule 10, PD 1096 Rule VII

questions.text: A designer proposes using reinforced concrete block (12-inch thick) as the separating wall between a paint storage room (Group G) and an adjacent office. What fire rating does this assembly typically provide?

options.text: No fire rating; concrete block must be tested per ASTM E119.

rationale.a: 1-hour is provided by a much thinner 4-inch block.
rationale.b: 2-hour is typically achieved by an 8-inch block.
rationale.d: Standard fire resistance tables (like those in the NBCP) provide established ratings for common masonry thicknesses.
rationale.correct: A 12-inch (300mm) thick concrete masonry unit wall typically provides a 4-hour fire rating per ASTM E119 tables, satisfying the Group G separation requirement.
rationale.takeaway: 12-inch CHB = 4-hour fire rating. This is the standard for hazardous occupancy separation.

questions.text: A high-rise office building has a central exit stairwell. Based on RA 9514 compartmentation rules, which of the following stairwell designs would be INCORRECT?

options.text: 2-hour rated walls on all four sides with 1-hour rated exit doors, ensuring compliance with fire safety standards for high-rise buildings
2-hour rated walls with 1-hour rated doors adjacent to office spaces, providing adequate fire separation and egress safety
2-hour reinforced concrete walls with 1-hour fire-rated steel exit doors, which are standard for maintaining structural integrity during a fire
2-hour rated walls on three sides and 1-hour rating on the adjacent mechanical room wall.

rationale.a: Correct: 2-hour walls and 1-hour doors are standard for high-rise egress.
rationale.b: Correct: Matches the requirements for a protected vertical exit.
rationale.c: Correct: Concrete and steel are common materials for achieving these ratings.
rationale.d: Incorrect: You cannot reduce the rating of the stairwell wall just because it faces a mechanical room; it must be 2-hour throughout.
rationale.correct: An exit enclosure must be continuous and maintain its rated integrity (2 hours for high-rise) on all sides. Reducing any portion of the enclosure wall to 1-hour violates the fire safety of the egress path.
rationale.takeaway: Exit enclosures must maintain their minimum required rating (2-hours for 4+ stories) on all surrounding walls.

questions.text: A Group D (storage) space is located adjacent to a Group B (office) space in a mixed-use building. According to PD 1096 and RA 9514, what is the minimum fire rating required for the separating wall?

rationale.a: 1-hour is the standard for corridor ratings, not for storage occupancy separation.
rationale.c: 3-hour is not a standard code rating for this specific separation.
rationale.d: 4-hour is required for Group G (high-hazard) separations.
rationale.correct: Group D (storage) separation from other occupancies requires a 2-hour minimum fire-rated wall per PD 1096 Table VII.4 and RA 9514 fire compartmentation rules.
rationale.takeaway: Occupancy separation for Storage (Group D) is 2-hours. Memorize: Corridor=1hr, Storage=2hr, Hazardous=4hr.

questions.code_citation: PD 1096 Rule VII Table VII.4, RA 9514 IRR Rule 10

questions.text: A multi-story office building has a central exit stairwell. The architect specifies 1-hour rated walls for the stairwell enclosure. Is this compliant with RA 9514?

options.text: Yes, 1-hour is sufficient for exit stairs.
No, exit stairs require 2-hour rated walls.
No, exit stairs require 3-hour rated walls.
No, exit stairs do not require fire-rated walls at all.

rationale.a: 1-hour is only permitted for enclosures connecting three stories or less.
rationale.c: 3-hour exceeds the standard requirement for stairwell enclosures.
rationale.d: All exit stairs must be enclosed in fire-rated assemblies to serve as a protected path of egress.
rationale.correct: Exit stairwell enclosures for buildings four stories or more must have a fire resistance rating of 2 hours per RA 9514 IRR Section 10.2.5.2.
rationale.takeaway: Vertical exit enclosures require 2-hour fire resistance in multi-story buildings (4+ floors).

questions.text: A laboratory building contains a paint storage room (Group G, high-hazard) adjacent to a research office (Group B). What is the required fire-rating for the separating wall?

options.text: No rating required; the rooms are on the same floor.

rationale.a: 2-hour applies to Group D (ordinary storage), not high-hazard Group G.
rationale.b: 3-hour is not the code standard for high-hazard separation.
rationale.d: Floor location does not waive the requirement for occupancy separation.
rationale.correct: Group G (High Hazard) occupancies must be separated from any other occupancy by a minimum of a 4-hour fire-rated wall per PD 1096 Table VII.4.
rationale.takeaway: Group G (Hazardous) separation is the most stringent at 4-hours.
